quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does a steady green light mean at an intersection?

options.text: You must slow down and be ready to stop.
You must stop and check for traffic before going.
You can go through if the road is clear.
You cannot turn right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you can drive through the intersection if the road is clear. You can also turn right or left unless a sign says you cannot. Always yield to other vehicles and pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: Which of these must you obey over the others?

options.text: A steady red light
A police officer
A stop sign
A flashing red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take precedence over all signs and signals. This includes police officers, fire police, flag persons in work zones, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: When can a driver legally pass on the right side of another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
Even if you have to drive off the road.
On a narrow bridge.
At any time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a passing lane available.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right if there is a passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left or waiting to turn left. You can also pass on the right on multi-lane roads with lanes going the same direction. Never drive off the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: How should head restraints be adjusted?

options.text: So they touch the back of the head.
Remove them from the seats if possible.
So they sit above the head.
They do not matter where they are.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they touch the back of the head.
questions.explanation: Head restraints should be adjusted to touch the back of the head. This helps prevent injury during crashes, sudden stops, and quick turns.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching railroad tracks?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks there are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you approach railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop for trains or other vehicles using the tracks.

questions.question: What blood alcohol level is illegal for drivers 21 or older?

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.
0.1 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: Drivers 21 or older cannot have a blood alcohol level of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are not working due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then proceed with caution.

questions.question: What must you do immediately when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and lights on?

options.text: Move to the right and stop.
Move to the right and slow down.
Move to the right and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop and let it pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses its lights and siren, you must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The vehicle coming from the right.
The vehicle coming from the left.
The vehicle that honks first.
The vehicle traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to any vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: Keeping a safe distance allows you to react to problems without hard braking. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when the way is clear.
You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until the light turns green or a green arrow appears. Unless a sign says otherwise, this rule always applies.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street without using its emergency lights or siren. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using lights or a siren, you do not need to move. Keep driving normally.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol at a social event, what is the safest way to drive home?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with someone who hasn't been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Stop drinking 30 minutes before you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with someone who hasn't been drinking.
questions.explanation: Ask a friend who hasn't drunk alcohol to drive you home. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your body. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and be careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of danger ahead. Slow down and look carefully before you proceed.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to avoid it.
Stop right away and block its path.
Move to the side and give it a clear path.
Signal when it is safe for it to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the side and give it a clear path.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the side of the road if it is safe. Give it plenty of room to pass.

questions.question: What should you do with loose objects in your car?

options.text: Put them on the back seat.
Put them on the floor near the driver's seat.
Secure them so they don't become a hazard.
Keep them on the back shelf.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure them so they don't become a hazard.
questions.explanation: Secure all loose objects before driving. Items that roll or move can hit you or block the pedals in a sudden stop or crash.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Stopping too many times.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast in wet conditions, your tires cannot remove water from the road. They lose grip and your car slides on water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic light is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Heavy trucks often travel slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. On hills with limited visibility, it is illegal to pass. Use caution when following large trucks.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrians may cross here.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians may cross here.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When turning left on a multilane, one-way road or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn left from the left lane on multilane roads and highways.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?

options.text: Slow down gradually and check the rearview mirror.
Move into the left lane.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prepare for a left turn: signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. On a multilane road, move into the left lane before the intersection. Wait for traffic and pedestrians to pass, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A roundabout is ahead.
Lane ends, merge left.
Turn around.
Curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A roundabout is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a roundabout is coming. Enter a roundabout slowly and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Press your brakes hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Use the parking brake.
Pump your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: On a slippery road, first release the gas pedal. If you need to slow down more, gently press the brake pedal with steady, light pressure.
